full_judgment:
2. The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 47 of 1978 for partition of the suit property against the petitioner and opposite party Nos. 2-11 alleging, inter alia, that the suit property consists of three plots, namely, plot Nos. 29, 40 and 41 appertaining to RS Khatian Nos. 568 and 960 of Mouja No. 118, Faridpur Town, along with structures threreon which originally belonged to Narayan Chandra Tahbilder, predecessor in interest of defendant Nos. 4-9 to the extent of 1I3rd share, Bhupati Mohan Tahbilder, Reboti Mohan Tahbilder and Parbati Mohan Tahbilder, the three brother to the extent of 1/3rd share, and Ranajit Mohan Tahbildar and Horipada Tahbildar, two brothers, to the extent of other 1/3rd share. Thus, the three sets of Tahbildars owned the suit property. Khatian No. 568 consists of two plots, namely, plot Nos. 39 and 41, and Khatian No. 960 consists of one plot, namely, plot No. 40. There is a building consisting of twelve rooms standing on plot Nos. 39 and 40 and the land appertaining to plot No. 41 is used as pathway which lies to the east of the aforesaid building. The area of .1079 acres of land appertaining to lot No. 39 has been acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 3/1964-65 before the purchase made by the parties, that is, the plaintiff and the opposite party Nos. 1-3. The further case of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 is that Rajanit Mohan Tahbildar sold his 1/6th share of plot No. 40 along with structure thereon to the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 vide registered deed dated 5-10-1970. Thereafter Horipada Tahbilder, the other brother of Ranajit, sold 478 of land of plot No. 39 and .003-3/4 acres of land of plot No. 41 and .0100 acres of land of plot No. 40 along with the structures standing thereon to the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 by another registered deed dated 7-2-1974, and thus the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 became the owner of the land along with the structures thereon as described in schedule 'ka' of the plaint and was possessing the same by mutating his name and on payment of rent regularly. The defendants Nos.1-3 have purchased land along with the structures thereon out of the said property from the original owners. The defendant petitioner purchased. 10 178 acres of land of plot No. 39 along with the structures thereon from Ranajit Mohan Tahbildar by a registered deed dated 17-7-1969 and before purchase he was possessing the same as tenant under the Tahbildar brothers and at the time of selling the suit property to the plaintiff opposite party No.1 the Tahbildar brothers disclosed the fact to the plaintiff and asked the defendant petitioner to pay rent to the plaintiff opposite party, and accordingly, the plaintiff opposite party got possession of the suit land through tenant, namely, the defendant No. 1 petitioner. During the liberation war the defendant petitioner left the country and, as such, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 took over possession and after the liberation of the country when the defendant petitioner came back to this country he restored possession of the suit land and he is in possession of the same and, as such, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 filed the instant suit for partition of his share. 

 5. It appears from the record that during the pendency of the suit an application under section 4 of the Partition Act was filed on 17-4-1986 by the defendant-petitioner and the said application was rejected by the trial Court and the defendant petitioner did not move the higher court against the aforesaid order. However, the trial Court after recording evidence and hearing the parties vide its judgment and decree dated 30-4-1986 decreed the suit in part in preliminary form on contest against the petitioner and opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 and ex parte against others without costs, and the trial Court found that the plaintiff opposite party No.1 is entitled to get a separate allotment for .0402 acres of land out of the suit khatian and also 1/6 the share of the building standing on the suit land, and defendant No.1 petitioner was given a separate allotment for .0402 acres of land out of the suit khatian and 1/6th share of the building standing thereon. Being aggrieved by the preliminary decree, the defendant petitioner preferred an appeal, being Title Appeal No. 121 of 1986 before the learned District Judge, Faridpur, and the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 also filed a cross objection thereto. The learned appellate Court below after hearing the parties dismissed the appeal of the defendant petitioner and allowed the cross objection filed by the plaintiff opposite party No.1 and accordingly. modified the decree by making allotment of .0298 acres of land with construction thereon in favour of the defendant petitioner and allotment of .0298 acres of plot No. 39.0200 acres of land of plot No. 40 and .0022 acres of plot No. 41 together with the construction thereon in favour of the plaintiff opposite party and allotment of remaining 1/3rd share of plot No. 39 and plot Nos. 40 and 41 together with the construction there on in favour of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 2 and 3. The defendant petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below preferred a revisional being Civil Revision No. 596 of 1989 before this court in which Rule was issued but finally, the Rule was discharged vide judgment dated 14-5-1992. Thereafter, against the said Judgment the present petitioner moved the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 344 of 1992 which was dismissed by the Appellate Division by order dated 27-4-1993. Thus, the preliminary decree of the aforesaid partition suit reached its finality and the record of the case was sent back to the trial Court. Thereafter, on 30-5-1993 the defendant petitioner again fi led an application under section 4 of the Partition Act to buy up the share of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1. The learned trial Court heard the said application on 5-8-1993 and by its order dated 7-8-1993 rejected the same without entering into merits of the application solely on the ground that earlier also an application was filed by the defendant petitioner before the trial Court and the said application was rejected by the predecessor judge of the court and as such, rejected the same. It further appears that thereafter on 7-9-1993 the defendant petitioner filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for hearing his application filed under section 4 of the Partition Act on 30-5-1993 on merit and the said application along with written objection filed by the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 were also heard and disposed of by the trial Court vide its order No. 161 dated 6-4-1994 and the trial Court was pleased to reject the defendant petitioner's application as the trial Court did not find any merit in the said application. The defendant petitioner then moved this court in revision against the order No. 106 dated 17-4-1986, order No. 132 dated 7-8-1993 and order No. 161 dated 6-4-1994, being Civil Revision No. 2624 of 1994, and that revisional application was heard and disposed of vide Judgment dated 11-7-1994 whereby a single bench of this Court set aside the impugned orders and sent back the case to the trial Court for disposing of the application filed under section 4 of the Partition Act on merit. Thus, the learned trial Court after hearing the parties vide his Judgment and order dated 9-10-1995 rejected the said application dated 30-5-1993 and being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 9-10-1995 the defendant petitioner moved this court in revision and obtained the instant Rule. 

 6. Mr Khandkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant petitioner, submits that the finding of the trial Court that the defendant petitioner did not purchase any land appertaining to plot No. 40 of Khatian No. 960 is erroneous as the trial Court failed to construe the title deed Exhibit 'Ka' along with the Town Survey Map and the holding number as mentioned in Exbit 'Ka' which clearly shows that the defendant petitioner in fact purchased land appertaining to both the plot Nos. 39 and 40 of Khatian Nos. 568 and 960. The learned Advocate further submits that the defendant petitioner purchased 1/6th share of the undivided dwelling house of the Tahbildar family by registered deed as back as in 1969 and after his purchase the other members of the undivided Tahbildar family did not raise any objection against the said purchase nor did they come up with any application under section 4 of the Partition Act to buy up the share of the defendant petitioner and, as such, the defendant petitioner was accepted as a member of the Tahbildar family and by virtue of this he also stepped into the shoes of the other members of the Tahbildar family and thereby he is entitled to file an application under section 4 of the Partition Act to buy up the share of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1. The learned Advocate further submits that the finding of the trial Court that the house in question is not at all a dwelling house of the Tahbildar family is erroneous and contrary to materials and evidence on record and it was also not proper for the trial Court to arrive at such a finding relying on the notes appearing in the book, "Law on Partition ", Third Edition, published by Dhaka Law Reports, without citing the case law or elaborating the facts therein which has caused a failure in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the superior courts of this sub-continent liberally construed section 4 of the Partition Act, and in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 30 Indian Cases 936, 97 Indian Cases 416 and AIR, 1963 (Cal) 161. 

 8. On a perusal of the impugned order it appears that the learned trial Court rejected the application of the defendant petitioner filed under section 4 of the Partition Act on three grounds. The learned trial Court arrived at a finding that from a perusal of the materials and evidence on record it cannot be said that the defendant petitioner has purchased any land appertaining to plot No. 40 of Khatian No. 960. The learned trial Court further observed that the structures standing on plot Nos. 39 and 40 was never the undivided dwelling house of the Tahbildar family, and in arriving at such a finding the learned trial Court observed that the members of the Tahbildar family after construction of the building in the said plot let out the same to different tenants and never used that house as their dwelling house nor anyone of them ever lived there. The learned trial Court also rejected the aforesaid application on the ground that the defendant petitioner by virtue of his purchase of a portion of the suit land in 1969 from Rajajit Tahbildar did not become a member of the undivided Tahbildar family although he has become a co-owner or co-sharer in the suit property. 

 11. In view of the materials and evidence on record it is difficult to accept the first submission of Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, vide Ext 'ka' that his client purchased four rooms of the twelve-roomed building standing on plot No. 40 appertaining to Khatian No. 960. The same argument, it appears, was canvassed by Mr Mahbubuddin Ahmed before the Appellant Division in the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 344 of 1992 and their Lordships after taking into consideration the materials and evidence on record observed that, "However, we have considered the documents and the map ourselves, which was difficult though without the help of a survey knowing Advocate, to ensure that the petitioner was deprived of his legitimate share on the basis of the kabala but we find it almost impossible to hold that the schedule of the document can plainly be construed to include part of the structures standing on plot No. 40 as contended by the learned Advocate. I have already mentioned that the share of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 was increased and that of the defendant petitioner was reduced in the appeal by the learned District Judge and against that the defendant petitioner preferred a revisional application before this court wherein the Rule was ultimately discharged by a single bench of this court upholding the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below, and against that Judgment and decree of this court the defendant petitioner preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 344 of 1992 in which their Lordships of the Appellate Division observed as quoted above. Besides, it is crystal clear from Ext 'ka' that the defendant petitioner has purchased 1/6th share of Ranajit Mohan Tahbildar appertaining to plot No. 39 of Khatian No. 568. It is also clear from a perusal of Ext 'ka' that the defendant petitioner purchased land from plot No. 39 with the structure thereon and the finding of the trial Court on this point is based on materials and evidence on record. Besides, this point has been finally decided by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 344 of 1992 and, as such, there is no scope for Mr Mahbubuddin Ahmed to reagitate that the finding of the appellate Court is erroneous on that point.
